Definition: dust (as powdered or gray); hence, clay, earth, mud
BiblicalUsage: Dust — God forming man from the dust of the ground, the sentence that dust we are and to dust we shall return, Abraham calling himself dust and ashes before the Lord, and Job repenting in dust and ashes. The word is our beginning, our end, and our confession.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe dust keeps me honest: I am made from it, I return to it, and the God who breathed life into it is the only reason dust can speak at all. Job's repentance in dust is where my pride ends and my hope begins.
